chunks: He will direct desires towards (the path of) guidance while people will have turned guidance towards desires, and he will turn their views to the direction of the Qur’ān while the people will have turned the Qur’ān to their views.

key_terms.الْهَوَى: Desire or whims (often negative, referring to base desires)

ai.seo_question: How does the Mahdi's approach to guidance and the Qur'an differ from that of the people?
ai.summary: In the context of Nahj al-Balagha's eschatological discourses, this saying highlights the Mahdi's role as the restorer of divine order by reversing the epistemological corruption of the age. While the masses subject the Qur'an to their subjective *ra'y* (opinion) and align guidance with fleeting *hawa* (desire), the Mahdi ensures that reason serves revelation and desires are subordinated to truth, fulfilling the Shia expectation of justice through the re-establishment of authentic interpretation.
